content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I'm using [product_name] V14 and attempting to connect via ethernet to a [product_name] module. The LAN indicator on the [product_name] alternates colors, but my PC shows a different status. I've tried multiple functional cables. I opened a new project to detect the unspecified CPU, as suggested by an online video, but I get no response from the [product_name] module. Is there a setting on the [product_name] itself needed for communication? Is direct programming of [product_name] possible with this software? Any advice is welcome. Thanks, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], What are the IP address and subnet mask of the [product_name] module? And of your PC? The [product_name] software does not support direct configuration of [product_name]. You need specialized software called [product_name] Comfort, latest version being V8.2.

I'm not sure about the [product_name], since this project hasn't started. The PC IP is 192.168.0.10, subnet mask 255.255.255.0. How can I get the [product_name] details if I can't connect? The detection always fails. Thanks for clarifying; I understand now that I need that specific software.
Sounds good. Which specific [product_name] module do you have? Please provide the complete [article_no]. Which [product_name] Comfort version are you using?

I've obtained the needed software and connected to the [product_name] using the PC. Its IP is now 192.168.0.107 and subnet is 255.255.255.0. Programming works fine. However, returning to the network, the device is still not detected with [product_name] V14. The requested number appears to be [article_no]. The first digits differ from available options in the detection menu. Info from direct connection: 8.FS4, software version V8.1.0.

[product_name] can't recognize [product_name] modules like it does other controllers. For [product_name] V14, [product_name] is almost like an external device. However, you can still use it for data exchange as it supports the same communication protocol as other controllers and HMIs. What is your intended use with the [product_name] connection?
I want to connect a [product_name] CPU. I tried selecting different CPUs from the dropdown menu, set the IP address, but couldn't establish a connection.

There are two possible ways to exchange data: - [product_name] acts as server, the controller as client. - [product_name] acts as client, the controller as server. It's generally easier if [product_name] is the client.
How can I set this up? See the attached file for more details.
I'm from Germany. I created examples for both data exchange methods for the German part of the forum. Let me know if you'd like me to upload both examples.
I'm also German. You can upload those examples, please.
Check out this topic in the German forum: Example: Setting up communication between [product_name] and [product_name] controller.
Thank you! I'll look into it.
You're welcome. If anything is unclear, feel free to ask.

Good morning all! I've tried more solutions overnight. Now, I can communicate with both the controller and the [product_name] using a single connection (no plugging/unplugging needed), and I can upload, download, and monitor both. However, the devices can't identify each other or share data. I followed the German guide closely, but the subnet settings didn't work. I've attached screenshots to illustrate the problem. Much appreciated.
Your screenshot shows [product_name] as server and the controller as client. Is that your goal?

Hello! I'm not completely sure. There is an existing network of PLCs and HMIs; I want to add the [product_name] device and need to both read and write a few bits. Does this make sense? I've also tried swapping client/server settings, but couldn't connect to the network. Ideally, I'd like to select the communications for individual bits by mapping and then changing the relevant IP address. I'm also uncertain about the meaning of TASP.

It's difficult if you haven't defined your exact requirements. Without seeing the projects, it's hard to diagnose the issue. As mentioned earlier, I posted sample programs. Programming is different depending on whether [product_name] is the server or client.

Given all that, what do you suggest? I want to edit a few bits, but can't make major changes to the network since others are involved. Any advice? I realize the code changes depending on connection type, but I'm stuck as I can't detect the [product_name] over the network, even though direct PC connection works fine.

If you want to set up communication between two devices, you must plan how to do it first. You asked here because you're unsure. I've shown you two methods: 1) [product_name] as server, controller as client—this is more complex since it requires specific function blocks. 2) [product_name] as client, controller as server—this is simpler and doesn't need the same function blocks.

I've reviewed the GET/PUT instructions. They seem feasible, but I can't complete their function blocks because the device detection process never shows the [product_name] as accessible. Wait, I noticed the GET block's partner field allowed selecting the unspecified CPU, and it auto-filled with the [product_name]. I'll investigate further.

Okay, when I first opened the GET instruction, the partner field allowed me to select the unspecified CPU, which then displayed the [product_name]. But when adding a second GET or first PUT instruction, this didn't happen—the field stayed red and had no options. It seems communication works intermittently or I was just lucky initially.
Previously selectable fields are now greyed out and inaccessible.

Oh, you use the PUT and GET function blocks. I don't use those. Refer to the [company_name] FAQ: How to program the GET and PUT instructions in the user program of the controller to transfer more than 160 bytes of data?
I'll check that. Do you know why the behavior I described happened—specifically, the availability of the partner field which is now read-only?
No, I haven't worked with those specific function blocks.

I think that successful connection was coincidental. Now, the plan has changed—we are using the [product_name] as a Modbus client. Let's see how this goes. Thanks very much for your assistance. Have a great weekend!
You too!

Good morning! Here's an update. The intermittent GET/PUT communication was likely due to a MB_CLIENT instruction using the same IP address I needed, which was set up with [company_name] support due to prior issues connecting the [product_name] to PROFINET. I was unaware of this. Disabling MB_CLIENT allowed successful access to the [product_name]. Since the project advanced with MODBUS elsewhere, we kept that solution. I've learned a lot from this—thank you for your input! Have a great day! Thanks, [user_name]
Likewise, have a good one!

analysis.insight_summary: Users had trouble connecting a [product_name] module using [product_name] V14 and ethernet, incorrectly assuming it could be set up and programmed directly with this software. The realization that [product_name] modules require their own configuration software led to workflow difficulties, with attempts to detect the device failing until the correct tool was used. Confusion also arose around integrating [product_name] with specific controllers and structuring client-server data exchange.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to directly set up and program [product_name] hardware via [product_name] V14, detect devices easily, and enable seamless data exchange between [product_name] modules and CPUs.
